1 · The pillar names, bigger

“make the directions in the directions only slide bigger”

With two pillars the cards are half the slide wide and the name sat at the top of a large empty box — the type was sized for four cards and never re-sized for two. The name grows with the room now, and the card centres what it holds instead of stacking it at the top.

It scales rather than being set to one size

Four pillars still read as they do today; the type grows only where there is room for it. A unit with eight would not suddenly have huge names in narrow cards.

2 · The aspiration across the width, and This year first

What we are aiming at

“make the wining aspiration filing the width of the presentaion rather than being stuck in a box on the left … flip this year column with the 2027 so the this year column to come after the obcejtives”

The aspiration sat in the left half of a two-column grid whose right half holds End in mind — so on every unit without one, half the slide was empty and the sentence was broken across four short lines for no reason. It runs the full width now, with End in mind beneath it where a unit has one.

And the objectives table reads This year then By 2027, so the eye meets the number being worked towards this cycle first.

Delivered and Planned appear in two places, and they are spelled differently in each. So “keep just measures and execution” means one change on each:

I would keep it. Say the word and it goes with the rest.

4 · 40 %% — the doubling my own fix could not see

“same error of duplicated unit despite being reported correctly in the reporting but reading with the issue in the performance”

You are right on both halves, and the second half is the diagnosis. The reporting page shows the number alone with the unit as a fixed suffix beside it, so it looks correct whatever is stored — and what is stored on that row is the string 40 %%. Same residue as 8 M EGP M EGP, from before the joiner was corrected.

The fix I shipped yesterday split the unit on spaces, so it collapsed M EGP M EGP and could not see %%, which is one word. A rule that only catches the spaced spelling catches half the fault.

It matches a unit written twice with or without a gap now — and only where both halves are a unit the platform actually knows, because ^(.+?)\s*\1$ on its own reads mm as a doubled m and would turn five millimetres into five metres.

And it caught a regression I had introduced

Yesterday's version rebuilt the string with a space for any unit it did not recognise, so 40%% came out as 40 %% — a value made worse by the function that exists to tidy it. It never adds a separator now: the gap it puts back is the gap it found, and the only thing it does on its own is close one.
